sources.name: The Guardian
sources.summary: Himari/Berlin Philharmonic/Weigle/Wang (Decca) The programme feels a little safe but the 15-year-old Japanese violinist impresses in her debut recording of works by Wieniawski, Chopin, Godowsky and Sibelius When 13-year-old Himari Yoshimura took to the stage with the Berlin Philharmonic in March 2025, she became the youngest Asian soloist to appear with the orchestra in a subscription concert. A subsequent contract with Decca made her the label’s youngest-ever female signing. Her debut album features that Berlin performance of Wieniawski’s Violin Concerto No 1, alongside studio recordings of music by Chopin, Godowsky and Sibelius. What is immediately apparent is the technical security of her playing, combined with an easy lyricism across the instrument’s full range. The fearsome double stopping in the Wieniawski is impressive, with some supple dynamic phrasing in the upper register. Occasionally a leap to a high note comes up a hair’s breadth short, something absent from the studio recordings, but this is nevertheless a significant performance. She’s not entirely helped by Sebastian Weigle’s smooth but staid accompaniments. It’s not the greatest concerto and needs a lighter touch to give it some lift (compare Michael Rabin and Adrian Boult). Continue reading...
